meanings: Orvenna: the pair-name of Ormund and Penna, the wall-masters
derivation: pair-name (orrowen_v2 §3.10): first post Or- (Ormund) + second post Penn- softened as the second element of a compound (p > v) + the lintel -a, the dual; the rule that gives Halyna, Aldwena and Idrenna; the cradle-names are the Book notes' (notes_v3 §pair-names); unit S03 (I.4)

meanings: Jory (a name): Voss's friend of Eldhythe, who whistled; the Book's English writes its first sound with J
derivation: a name; names are names (orrowen_v2 §4.6). The tongue has no j (§2.5): the Book's Jory is /'jori/, and Orrowen's only /j/ is the y of the romanisation (§2.4), so the ink spells it Yory, as Seren's English spells it Jory; the leaf-hand writes its first letter as g with the softening bite (§6.3), the one name that carries a bite, because the hand has no other way to write the sound. Cross-unit [orchestrator]: every leaf that names Jory (I.3, I.5, IV.5, V.1, V.5) should take one form; unit S03 (I.5)

meanings: Ebba (a name): Old Ebba of Fenholm, Marl's grandmother, who first said the hearth's answer
derivation: a name; names are names (orrowen_v2 §4.6); the doubled b stands as in hebb, gebb; unit S03 (I.5)

meanings: a whistle, a tune whistled, a song with no words; to whistle ('breath-song')
derivation: compound (orrowen_v2 §3.10, §5.12): hoss 'breath' (canon) + vell 'song; sing' (O2698), the head second, v unchanged by the seam's softening; Jory 'whistled the tune and never the words', so a whistle is a song of the breath alone; VN hossvellyl (slender, after vell). Cross-unit: I.3, IV.5, V.1, V.5 whistle too; unit S03 (I.5)

meanings: a bench-end, the end of a bench
derivation: compound: prenth 'a bench' (O1988) + S·dask 'end' (d > r), as orlrask 'nightfall, the day's end' and surrask 'the year's end'; unit S03 (I.5)

meanings: raw, the skin rubbed off (of hands and fingers): un-skinned
derivation: na- (un-, +S) + sast 'skin, a hide; a crust' (O2209) + -At ('provided with X', as lernulat, sulvat): 'not provided with skin'; the children scrape the bloom, the stone's crust (sast stacorn), and lose their own; unit S03 (I.4)
